evidence: The mechanics are as described. find_signal_implementation_run (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:484-517) checks only run.team_id, task.signal_report_id is not None, and not task.internal (api.py:505-509); it never reads SignalReportTask.relationship, the signals task_run artefact type, or ai_stage. Discussion tasks do exist through a production path and do pass that test: the Inbox 'Discuss report' button (frontend/src/scenes/inbox/components/detail/DiscussReportButton.tsx:31-32 -> inboxTaskKickoffLogic.ts:170-181 -> createReportTask 46-97) calls api.tasks.create with origin_product=signal_report, signal_report=<report>, signal_report_task_relationship='discussion', and repository = the report's repo_selection artefact when one resolved (53-64; not required for discuss, 76-79), then api.tasks.run with run_source=signal_report (91-97). Server side, facade create_task (api.py:3660-3802) does Task.objects.create(**validated_data) (3788) with `internal` unset, so the model default False applies (products/tasks/backend/models.py:207-210), and record_report_task (products/signals/backend/task_run_artefacts.py:138-160) writes only a `task_run` artefact of type 'discussion' (no SignalReportTask row, which only the implementation branch at 120-126/148 writes). run_task (api.py:4306-4607) forces pr_authorship_mode=BOT for run_source=signal_report (4402-4403), stores no ai_stage (4405-4413), grants full MCP scopes (3167-3169), and dispatches via _trigger_task_processing_workflow (3154-3183) -> execute_task_processing_workflow whose create_pr defaults True (products/tasks/backend/temporal/client.py:163, 247). The discuss prompt ('Let's discuss this PostHog Inbox report: <url>\n\n<question>', inboxTaskKickoffLogic.ts:40-44) does not forbid code changes, so an agent that opens a PR gets bound by the webhook branch leg (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:64-79), has output.pr_url recorded for a repo-native head (webhooks.py:157-186), trips the review_hog receiver whose filter is the identical signal_report_id + not internal test (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:98-104, with the stale comment 'only the report's implementation task reviews'), and on later synchronize the stamphog carve-out (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:144-231) receives the facade DTO. Given KA9 (auto-start's real implementation task is internal=True, products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:244-261; research/repo-selection tasks likewise internal=True at report_generation/research.py:715-718 and logic/repo_selection/agent.py:437-440), the only tasks that pass this facade at this head are API-created signal-report tasks: the Inbox 'Create PR' (relationship=implementation) and 'Discuss' (relationship=discussion) tasks, plus anything a task:write caller creates. But the delta over LA15 is nil. The adversarial reading ('a PR from a discussion task bypasses the bot, draft, review-mode and permission gates') is exactly LA15's claim that the facade authorizes on caller-writable task attribution, and LA15 already lists that a member can create such a task themselves (serializers.py:407-460, 595-598, 616-619). The proposed fix (require SignalReportTask.relationship == 'implementation') closes nothing: the relationship is a client-asserted free-form identifier on the same create call (serializers.py:441-451, 622-640; help text says any routing-safe identifier is accepted), and omitting it defaults to 'implementation' and writes the SignalReportTask row (task_run_artefacts.py:148-149). The non-adversarial reading (an honest discussion agent that happens to open a PR is reviewed under self-driving provenance) carries the same trust class as the Inbox 'Create PR' task created by the byte-identical API call — team App bot author, repo-native head, report-linked, started by a team member, acting reviewer opted in via stamphog_review_inbox_prs — so it is a label mismatch against the AGENTS.md wording ('implementation run', products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:84-85) rather than a new gate bypass, and it lives equally in the receiver leg the finding does not mention. Tests (products/tasks/backend/tests/test_webhooks.py:1246-1320) vary only `internal`, never the relationship, so nothing pins either behavior.
notes: Duplicate: a sub-case of LA15 (the facade trusts caller-asserted task attributes; a discussion task is one honest instance of an API-created, internal=False, signal-report task). LA15's remedy — a server-recorded linkage such as the webhook backstop's _record_run_pr_url plus rejecting caller writes to output.pr_url/branch — subsumes this, while LB14's relationship check would be bypassed by the default relationship. Would become a standalone `consider` (not must_fix) only if the facade were first fixed to a server-recorded linkage and discussion runs were still meant to be excluded from self-driving review (e.g. if the stamphog_review_inbox_prs toggle is documented as implementation-PRs-only); it would be moot if discussion tasks were created with a distinct trust class (internal=True, no repository, or create_pr=False).
